subject: zoology
question_text: Write short notes on pneumonia and its prophylaxis.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.67, Star Q 187). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. SPELLING CORRECTED: the book prints the bacterial names as 'streptococcus pneumonia' and 'Haemophilus influenza'; the accepted binomials are Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae, which is what this card writes. ADDED BEYOND THE BOOK: the fluid-filled alveoli, the chest pain and the grey-to-blue lips and nails are standard NCERT and are not printed in this book's answer.

steps.label: The disease and its cause
lines: Pneumonia is a bacterial disease of the lungs.
It is caused by the gram positive bacteria
Streptococcus pneumoniae and by Haemophilus
influenzae.
These bacteria infect the alveoli of the lungs.
steps.why: The site of the infection is the alveoli, and that single fact explains both the symptom and the treatment written later in the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing that pneumonia is a viral disease. It is bacterial.
Naming the bacteria without the site. The alveoli are where they settle.
steps.memory_tip: Two bacteria, one site: Streptococcus and Haemophilus in the alveoli.
steps.margin_note: Three short lines: the disease, the two bacteria, the site.

steps.label: Mode of infection
lines: The infection spreads when a healthy person
inhales the aerosols, that is the fine droplets,
released by an infected person while coughing or
sneezing.
Sharing utensils with an infected person can
also pass on the infection.
steps.why: The route decides the prevention, so naming the droplets here is what makes masks and boiled utensils the obvious measures at the end.
common_mistakes: Writing that pneumonia spreads through water. It spreads through droplets in the air.
Leaving out the shared utensils, which is why boiled utensils appear in the prophylaxis.
steps.memory_tip: It travels in the air and on shared utensils, so masks and boiling stop it.

steps.label: Symptoms
lines: The infected alveoli fill with fluid, so the
exchange of gases is reduced.
The patient has severe difficulty in breathing,
with fever, cough and pain in the chest.
The lips and the finger nails may turn grey to
blue in a severe case.
steps.why: The breathing difficulty is not a separate fact: it follows straight from fluid filling the alveoli, so the two lines are written as cause and effect.
common_mistakes: Writing the symptoms without the fluid in the alveoli. The fluid is the reason for them.
Writing that pneumonia causes loose motions. It is a lung disease.
steps.memory_tip: Fluid in the alveoli means less gas exchange, so breathing becomes hard.
steps.margin_note: Three short lines: the fluid, the breathing, the severe signs.

steps.label: Prophylaxis
lines: Use masks, so the droplets are not inhaled.
Use boiled utensils, so the bacteria on shared
utensils are killed.
Vaccines are available and give protection.
Antibiotics are used to treat a patient who has
already been infected.
steps.why: Prophylaxis means stopping the disease before it starts, so the first three measures are preventive and the antibiotic is added last as treatment, not prevention.
common_mistakes: Listing only antibiotics. Antibiotics treat; masks, boiled utensils and vaccines prevent.
Writing 'keep clean' with no measure named.
steps.memory_tip: Block the route, then build the defence: masks and boiling first, vaccine next, antibiotic last.
steps.margin_note: Four named measures in the box, one line each. Closing mark.

insider_note: Prophylaxis is a separate mark from treatment, so name the preventive measures first and keep antibiotics to the end.
